about.text: I am a Ph.D. student at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Michael R. Lyu. My research focuses on AI 4 Infra & Infra 4 AI: building high-performance infrastructure for AI workloads (LLM inference and serving systems, GPU/accelerator systems, multi-GPU scheduling), and applying AI to make cloud and LLM-as-a-Service platforms fast, reliable, and operable.

projects.name: ASC Student Supercomputer Competition
projects.detail: Silver Prize (2/300+) — led the LLM inference acceleration challenge
points: Built a high-throughput LLM inference framework: fine-grained request scheduling and memory management for multi-GPU asynchronous pipeline parallelism, plus a heterogeneous load-balancing scheme for multi-GPU data parallelism

Optimized HPC applications: OpenCAEPoro (flow simulation) dynamic-to-static storage conversion with profiling; WannierTools (topological materials) matrix reuse and BLAS overhead reduction for matrix inversion

projects.name: CAS-PRA Parallel Application Competition
projects.detail: 1st Prize, Central-South Division — 1st place in both challenges (1/80+ and 1/60+)
points: Optimized neural-network systems on DCU (AMD GPU architecture), focusing on data flows and compute kernels: the Conv-2D kernel in CNN, and GEMM, SpMM, and Softmax kernels in GCN
Innovated a new SpMM algorithm inspired by the CSR-5 SpMV algorithm to accelerate GCN inference

projects.name: Matrix Multiplication Library for Phytium ARMv8 Processor
projects.detail: SYSU Undergraduate Training Program for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (Outstanding, 1/17)
points: Optimized GEMM at assembly level for FT2000-series ARMv8 (Aarch64) multi-core processors, outperforming existing BLAS libraries
Optimized SpGEMM for ARMv8, porting and optimizing the CSeg algorithm to ARM

projects.name: YatSen OS
points: Implemented an operating system in C++
Focused on virtual memory systems as an extra component: page replacement (LRU), page-fault handling, and disk swap-space management
Contributed to the design of the next-gen Rust OS lab, YatSenOS-v2

projects.name: YatCPU
points: Implemented a RISC-V processor in Chisel
Five-stage pipelined, single-issue, in-order processor supporting a subset of the RV32I integer instruction set

projects.name: CSAPP Course and Labs
points: Perfect scores across all labs, focusing on the most challenging Malloc Lab
Visualized heap memory usage and compared allocation strategies
Implemented a Segregated Free List with mini-blocks, similar to Linux's buddy system

AI Systems: LLM inference & serving, multi-GPU scheduling and memory management
Linux: supercomputer platforms (Tianhe, Sunway, Sugon), university clusters, edge devices; personal services on private cloud servers
